content.text:
The training view shows a clean structural split: decisions where fusion genuinely reduces work cluster at ratios ≤ 0.892 (large-producer matrix cases: producerElements 147k–29M, originalWork in the millions), while near-baseline decisions cluster at ratios ≥ 0.995 (small producerElements, elementwise chains — the row-scheduled regression candidates). The known staged program exposes the near-baseline cases too and relies on cleanup to repair them. My three hypotheses vary where the filtering happens:

1. **seq-loose-cleanup** — keep the proven expose, widen cleanup to 1.05 so row-scheduled regressions up to ~6% growth (e.g., the 1.0597-growth decision in example 5) are also recovered, while tiled-mapped contraction producers stay protected.
2. **seq-reduction-only** — expose only decisions with real work reduction (threshold 0.95 sits in the empty gap between 0.892 and 0.995), so near-baseline cases are never exposed at all and cleanup restores them exactly as the default would.
3. **seq-size-gated** — gate exposure by problem size: large-work decisions need ≥5% reduction (tiled potential), small-work decisions need ≥30% (launch overhead makes marginal fusion unattractive), cleanup at 1.02.
